draft.title: Effects of ionising radiation
card: Ionising radiation carries enough energy to knock electrons from atoms. In living tissue it can damage cells, including their DNA.
the energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue. It is measured in grays (Gy), where 1 Gy is 1 joule per kilogram.
absorbed dose adjusted for the type of radiation, as some types do more harm for the same energy absorbed. It is measured in sieverts (Sv).
equivalent dose adjusted for the tissue, as some tissues are more sensitive than others. It is also measured in sieverts (Sv).
draft.remember: Grays measure energy absorbed per kilogram. Sieverts allow for radiation type and tissue.

a.q: Which dose is measured in grays?
a.why: Absorbed dose is the energy absorbed per kilogram, and its unit is the gray. Equivalent and effective dose are adjusted for harm, so they use sieverts.

b.q: Two workers each absorb 2 mGy, one from one type of radiation and one from another that does more harm per unit of energy. How do their equivalent doses compare?
opts: They are the same, as absorbed doses match
They cannot be compared, as sieverts are not used
b.why: Equivalent dose allows for the type of radiation, so the type that does more harm gives a larger value. The matching absorbed doses are tempting, but they ignore the type.
b.clue: Which dose allows for the type of radiation?
